applies_why: The judge marks a point UNDERDETERMINED even though the stated reason shows the verse carrying two senses (a footed covenant-origin analogy and its own source statement), which the rule says is not open.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: 'not open' — read as 'not underdetermined' or 'not open to challenge'; the rule's contrast with STANDS/UNDERDETERMINED favors 'not underdetermined'.
why: The judge's UNDERDETERMINED verdict is grounded on Matthew 1:20 having a footed covenant-origin analogy alongside its own source statement, so it treats a two-sense verse as open contrary to K-S2.
